Re: Appeal of denial of hip arthroscopy  
Member: Skyler Grant  
Member ID: W988301014  
Reference number: POC-F65CAC945B-43805  
Requested procedure: Hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914  
Date of adverse benefit determination: August 3, 2026

To the Appeals Department:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914. Please accept this letter and the enclosed clinical records as my request for reconsideration and overturn the denial based on the documented medical necessity of the requested procedure.

I have had 14 months of progressive hip pain that has not resolved with rest. The pain is sharp and located in the anterior groin, particularly with sitting and pivoting. I cannot run or squat, and my affected-hip range of motion is limited by pain. Provocative testing on the affected side is positive.

I have completed substantial conservative treatment without adequate or lasting relief:

- Sixteen weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization and activity modification, from March 2, 2026, through June 22, 2026, with 18 visits completed. The physical therapy discharge note documents this treatment.
- NSAID treatment for six months, with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on May 4, 2026, which provided only three weeks of partial relief.

The June 23, 2026 MRI arthrogram provides objective evidence of the condition being treated. It shows an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement and an alpha angle of 68 degrees. The joint space is preserved, and the hip is Tönnis grade 0. These findings support a structural cause for the persistent symptoms and support arthroscopic treatment rather than continued unsuccessful conservative care.

The record also documents the absence of listed clinical factors that could complicate or contraindicate treatment: there is no active infection, no untreated substance use, and no smoking. BMI is 29. The requested procedure was submitted by Duval, MD, orthopedic surgery.

The denial notice does not identify the specific medical policy, policy number, version, effective date, or individual medical-necessity criteria applied to CPT 29914. I was unable to identify a governing policy from the information in the notice. Please provide the exact policy or clinical-review guideline used for this determination, including the version in effect for this request, every criterion applied, and the specific clinical information that was considered insufficient. Please also provide the complete clinical-review rationale and any records relied upon in making the determination.

Based on the documented persistent symptoms, failed conservative treatment, objective MRI arthrogram findings, preserved joint space, Tönnis grade 0 status, functional impairment, and orthopedic-surgery recommendation, I request that the plan reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 29914.

If the plan cannot approve the request on reconsideration, please treat this as a request for the applicable next level of appeal and provide written instructions for that process. Please send the appeal determination and the requested policy and review materials to:

Skyler Grant  
[Mailing address]  
[Telephone number]  
[Email address]

I understand from the notice that the appeal must be received by January 30, 2027. Please confirm receipt of this appeal and advise me promptly if any additional information is required.

Sincerely,

Skyler Grant
